changes.after: Downgrade is free and unlimited: an item can go to any level from 1 up to its current level, at any Blacksmith level (the old downgrade-reach rule is removed). Nothing is refunded. The item LOSES the stored levelling gold of the dropped levels (RESOLVED (USER) Q7): downgrading from level A to level B reduces its levelling credit by exactly the credit each dropped level (A, A−1, … B+1) added when it was last bought, most recent first. changes.before: When enchanting raises an item's rarity, the player pays the upgrade cost difference they skipped: what the item's Blacksmith upgrades from its starting level to its current level cost at the new rarity, minus what they cost at the old rarity (gold + gear-upgrade materials). Every route (upgrade then enchant, or enchant then upgrade) costs the same total while the Blacksmith level matches the item's level; when the Blacksmith is ahead of the item, enchanting late costs more (ACCEPTED - USER DECISION 2026-11-01: Common -> Epic L1-99 with the Blacksmith at L10 all game, 1H +2,760g, 2H +4,133g). Each item stores one extra saved number: the item level it dropped or was bought at. How it is worked out: for each level from the item's starting level to its current level, (normal Blacksmith upgrade cost at the new rarity - cost at the old rarity), gold and gear materials. Discount (LOCKED - USER DECISION 2026-11-01): each level uses the Blacksmith gold discount of the Blacksmith level needed to reach that level, 3% x (ceil(level / 10) - 1) - levels 2-10 0%, 11-20 3%, 21-30 6% ... 81-90 24%, 91-99 27% - NOT the player's current discount. changes.after: Each item saves a levelling record (equipment_schema 20): the free level F = the level the item arrived at (drop, shop, Black Market, recruit, starter; items that exist before the build = their current level; levels up to F were never paid for and carry 0 credit) plus at most 10 (highest item level, Blacksmith level) pairs in rising order, e.g. F = 12; (40, b4); (99, b10). R = rarity multiplier × 10 (Common 10, Uncommon 15, Rare 25, Epic 40, Exalted 55, Legendary 70, Mythic 120, Transcendent 200, Unique 150); Paid(C, R) = floor(C × R / 250,000). Items that exist before the build have C = 0, so they never owe catch-up for past levels.

changes.after: Expedition Fortune / 1.75. Unit Fortune = LUK / (LUK + 200) + flat bonuses (Lucky traits; gear Fortune lines +0.05 / +0.10 / +0.15 / +0.20); no per-unit limit. Expedition Fortune = highest Unit Fortune + 50% of the 2nd + 25% of the 3rd. CLAMP (explicit rule): after every Fortune bonus is added (unit LUK, traits, gear lines, Fountain, Idol of Fortune, and the Thief single-reward bonus, which comes last) Expedition Fortune is clamped to 0-1.75, applied again after each bonus. So Normalized Expedition Fortune is at most 1.00: Fortune Multiplier at most ×2.00 (rows 12, 13) and Gold Multiplier at most ×1.50 (rows 17, 28). The lower limit 0 stops Unlucky traits making drops worse than base.

Gear alone needs 9 T4 Fortune lines across 3 units to reach the cap (7 with Lucky (Greater) on all 3; 4 with the Fountain or Idol of Fortune); T1/T2 lines alone never reach it; natural Fortune gems alone reach about ×1.53 (top 10% ×1.73). Simulator 300,000 builds: never above ×2.00 / ×1.50, never below ×1.00, provided the clamp is re-applied after the Thief bonus (implementation_plan 53).
